grounded_facts: Stephanie reviews documents and discovers that Mrs. Ganush's home is being repossessed due to delinquent payments.
memories.memory_text: I saw Stephanie reviewing the documents I gave her, and I heard her say they were a delinquency notice and a court order for repossession, telling me the bank intended to take my home tomorrow.

grounded_facts: Stephanie pleads with Mr. Jacks to grant Mrs. Ganush a loan extension due to her hardship.
memories.memory_text: I asked Stephanie to help me get an extension on my mortgage because I'm on a fixed income and have had medical problems, and they're trying to take my home.

grounded_facts: Mr. Jacks refuses to approve a further extension on Mrs. Ganush's loan, citing bank policy and financial incentives.
memories.memory_text: I was told that Mr. Jacks refused to approve another extension, saying the bank already gave me two and that they make money from the fees.

grounded_facts: After failing to secure approval, Stephanie informs Mrs. Ganush that no further extension can be granted.
memories.memory_text: I was told by Stephanie that another extension on my loan was out of the question.

grounded_facts: Mrs. Ganush kneels and begs Stephanie for mercy, invoking her pride and mother's grave.
memories.memory_text: I knelt before Stephanie and begged her for mercy, invoking my pride and my mother's grave, hoping she would understand how desperate I am.

grounded_facts: Mrs. Ganush asks Stephanie to help stop the repossession of her home.
memories.memory_text: I asked Stephanie to help me stop the repossession of my home, and I begged her for mercy, even humbling myself because I am a proud woman but desperate to keep my house.

grounded_facts: Mrs. Ganush kneels, clutches Stephanie's leg, and begs for mercy, then is shamed when rejected and attempts to take Stephanie's bracelet.
memories.memory_text: I clutched Stephanie's leg and begged her, refusing to let go even when she tried to pull away, and when she rejected me, I felt the shame burn through me before I reached for her bracelet.

grounded_facts: After being rejected, Mrs. Ganush grabs Stephanie's arm and attempts to take her charm bracelet, implying a symbolic or supernatural retaliation.
memories.memory_text: After she turned me down, I grabbed her arm and tried to take her charm bracelet, feeling like I had nothing left to lose.

grounded_facts: Security removes Mrs. Ganush after she refuses to release Stephanie and attempts to take her bracelet.
memories.memory_text: I refused to release Stephanie, and when I tried to take her bracelet, security intervened and escorted me out.

grounded_facts: Mrs. Ganush visits the Bank of California to seek help preventing the repossession of her home.
memories.memory_text: I went to the Bank of California to ask for help so they wouldn't take my home, and I begged Stephanie Brown to give me more time, even though I'm a proud woman and have never asked for anything like that before.

grounded_facts: Mrs. Ganush suddenly emerges from hiding in the back seat of Stephanie's car and attacks.
memories.memory_text: I suddenly emerged from hiding in the back seat of Stephanie's car and attacked her.

grounded_facts: Mrs. Ganush shrieks in Hungarian, threatening to pluck out Stephanie's eyes.
memories.memory_text: I shrieked at Stephanie in Hungarian that I would pluck out her eyes.

grounded_facts: Stephanie jams colored push pins into Mrs. Ganush's arm to break her chokehold.
memories.memory_text: I felt a sharp pain in my arm when she jammed those colored push pins into me, and my grip loosened as a result.

grounded_facts: Stephanie uses a stapler to strike Mrs. Ganush multiple times in the forehead, temporarily impairing her.
memories.memory_text: I was struck multiple times in the forehead with a stapler, each blow driving a staple into my skin, and I howled in pain while still trying to hold on.

grounded_facts: Stephanie accelerates the car, causing it to crash into a concrete column, violently throwing Mrs. Ganush forward.
memories.memory_text: I was thrown forward violently when Stephanie accelerated the car into a concrete column, and I crashed hard against the dashboard.

grounded_facts: After the crash, Stephanie opens the passenger door and shoves Mrs. Ganush out, then reverses to block her re-entry.
memories.memory_text: I was still dazed from the crash when Stephanie suddenly opened the passenger door and shoved me out with her foot; I hit the ground hard, but I got back up and tried to climb into the car again, only for her to reverse and knock me down with the door, then lock me out while I pulled at the handle in fury.

grounded_facts: Stephanie declares victory and mocks Mrs. Ganush with a reference to Geritol.
memories.memory_text: I heard Stephanie shout that she beat me and mock me by telling me to take my Geritol next time.

grounded_facts: Mrs. Ganush breaks the car window and bites Stephanie's chin, gumming it with her toothless mouth.
memories.memory_text: I broke the car window with a chunk of concrete and bit Stephanie's chin, gumming it with my mouth even as she shoved a ruler down my throat and I struggled to hold on.

grounded_facts: Mrs. Ganush plucks a brass button from Stephanie's coat and invokes the name 'Lamia', prophesying Stephanie's downfall.
Mrs. Ganush removes a button from Stephanie's coat and invokes the name 'Lamia', predicting Stephanie's suffering.
memories.memory_text: I reached out and plucked a brass button from Stephanie's coat, then held it up and whispered 'Lamia...'—I told her it begins tonight when she hears the cry, and that the Lamia is coming for her.

grounded_facts: A violent and supernatural encounter between Stephanie and Mrs. Ganush in a deserted parking structure after work.
memories.memory_text: I attacked Stephanie in her car, screaming at her in Hungarian that I would pluck out her eyes, and I clawed at her face and throat; when she fought back and shoved me out, I got back up despite my injuries, limped to the car, tried to get in, then smashed the window with a chunk of concrete; I reached inside, grabbed her legs and dragged her onto the pavement, but when I stood over her, I could only wheeze; I held up her button and whispered 'Lamia...' to curse her, telling her the Lamia was coming for her, and then I vanished as she swatted at a fly and grew dizzy.

grounded_facts: After the curse, Stephanie becomes dizzy, leans on the car, and upon recovering, finds Mrs. Ganush gone.
memories.memory_text: I saw Stephanie grow dizzy and lean against the car, and when she looked up, I was already gone.

grounded_facts: The iron gate outside Stephanie's house opens by itself, producing a shrieking sound.
The kitchen windows suddenly swing open due to supernatural force.
memories.memory_text: I saw the iron gate outside Stephanie's house tear open with a shriek, and the kitchen windows suddenly swung open—all by themselves, as if some unseen force had wrenched them wide.

grounded_facts: A shadow on the wall briefly takes the form of Mrs. Ganush's silhouette despite no one being present.
memories.memory_text: I saw my silhouette form in the shadow on the wall, even though I wasn't physically there.

grounded_facts: An invisible force begins physically assaulting Stephanie, starting with a strike to the face.
An unseen entity lifts and throws Stephanie against the wall, causing her to fall to the floor.
memories.memory_text: I felt an invisible force strike me in the face, making my mouth bleed, and then I was suddenly lifted and thrown against the wall before crashing to the floor.

grounded_facts: Stephanie awakens in bed, gasping, after experiencing a nested nightmare involving Mrs. Ganush attacking her.
memories.memory_text: I was in Stephanie's bed, covered in black flies, and I lunged at her with my teeth, clamping my hands around her throat and shaking her as she tried to push me away, but I could feel her weakening as I closed in on her face.

grounded_facts: Ray tells Stephanie that Doctor Rangervertz is available during her lunch hour.
Ray informs Stephanie she can see Doctor Rangervertz during her lunch hour, offering a solution to her distress.
memories.memory_text: I was told that Doctor Rangervertz is available during my lunch hour, and I could see him to help with my distress.

grounded_facts: Stephanie proposes to return Mrs. Ganush's house and belongings on behalf of the bank, requesting that Mrs. Ganush revoke the curse she placed on her.
Stephanie asks Mrs. Ganush to remove the curse she placed, offering to restore her home and possessions.
memories.memory_text: She told me she could return my house and all my things, and asked me to cancel the curse I placed on her as if it were nothing.

grounded_facts: A meeting initiated by Stephanie in Mrs. Ganush's living room where she attempts to negotiate the reversal of a curse in exchange for restitution of the house.
memories.memory_text: I was in my living room when Stephanie showed up, trying to make some kind of deal with me about my house and what she called a mistake by the bank.

grounded_facts: Mrs. Ganush refuses Stephanie's offer, stating that she now wants Stephanie to suffer due to the shame she endured.
Mrs. Ganush explicitly states that she no longer wants restitution but instead wants Stephanie to suffer due to past humiliation.
memories.memory_text: I told Stephanie it was what I wanted before she shamed me, and now I want to see her suffer.

grounded_facts: Stephanie hurries to her car and drives away from Mrs. Ganush's house after the encounter.
memories.memory_text: I heard my cackling echo as Stephanie hurried to her car and drove off from my house.

grounded_facts: Stephanie admits to Ilenka that she personally denied Sylvia Ganush's loan application in order to advance her career, acknowledging it was wrong and expressing shame.
memories.memory_text: I learned that Stephanie admitted to denying my loan application to get ahead at work, saying it was wrong and that she was ashamed, begging me to forgive her.

grounded_facts: Ilenka confronts Stephanie, accusing her of being the bank employee who took her grandmother's house, seeing through her excuses.
memories.memory_text: I heard Ilenka confront Stephanie, telling her that she knew she was the one from the bank who took my house and caused me great pain, saying she wasn't welcome here.

grounded_facts: Stephanie pushes through the party and accidentally falls on Sylvia Ganush's corpse, realizing for the first time that Sylvia is dead.
memories.memory_text: I was pushing through the crowd at the wake when I stumbled and fell right on top of her—Mrs. Ganush's corpse. I didn't even know she was dead until that moment.

grounded_facts: A traditional Gypsy wake held in honor of Sylvia Ganush, where her body lies uncoffined on a coffee table and mourners gather to drink, gamble, and pay respects.
memories.memory_text: I remember my body lying on the coffee table during the wake, hearing the hip hop and laughter around me as mourners gathered to pay their respects according to our traditions.

grounded_facts: Ilenka tells the crowd that Stephanie is responsible for her grandmother's downfall and publicly brands her as bearing the curse of Lamia.
memories.memory_text: I heard Ilenka tell the crowd that Stephanie was responsible for my downfall and that she now bears the curse of Lamia.

grounded_facts: After Ilenka's declaration, mourners react with disgust: one spits at Stephanie, another shields her child and kisses a crucifix.
memories.memory_text: I saw the mourners react to Stephanie with disgust—someone spat at her feet, and a mother shielded her child and kissed a crucifix.

grounded_facts: Ilenka confirms that Stephanie now bears the curse of Lamia and declares it will never be removed, reinforcing her grandmother’s judgment.
memories.memory_text: I remember Ilenka confirming that the curse of Lamia is on Stephanie and declaring it will never be removed, just as I had judged.

grounded_facts: After Ilenka says 'maybe she can...', Stephanie sees that Sylvia Ganush's corpse has turned its head and opened its eyes, staring directly at her.
memories.memory_text: I saw the corpse turn its head and open its eyes, staring right at me after Ilenka said maybe she could still see me.

grounded_facts: Rham Jas teaches Stephanie a chant to open herself to spirits, preparing her for the ritual.
memories.memory_text: I saw Rham Jas teach Stephanie the chant 'I welcome the dead into my soul' to prepare her for the ritual.

grounded_facts: After biting Milos, the Lamia spirit transfers from the goat into Milos, who becomes violently possessed.
memories.memory_text: I saw the goat bite Milos's hand, and then his eyes turned black like a goat's—he screamed and shouted at Stephanie in a voice that wasn't his.

grounded_facts: Rham Jas attempts to command the Lamia to depart from Milos' body.
memories.memory_text: I saw Rham Jas try to command the Lamia to leave Milos's body, but a chair flew and knocked him down before he could finish.

grounded_facts: The spirit of Mrs. Ganush appears and physically attacks Stephanie, scratching her and ripping out her hair.
memories.memory_text: I reached down and scratched at Stephanie's face, floating above her, and I tore out a clump of her hair when she tried to pull away.

grounded_facts: Shaun San Dena performs a chant that forcibly removes the Lamia spirit from Milos, causing him intense pain but freeing him.
memories.memory_text: I reached down and clawed at Stephanie’s face, screaming at her to make her stop the chanting, and when I tore out a clump of her hair and vomited up her dead cat, I saw the white vapor ripped from Milos as the Lamia left him and he collapsed, finally free.

grounded_facts: After expelling the Lamia, Shaun San Dena collapses, stops breathing, and dies despite CPR attempts.
memories.memory_text: I saw Shaun San Dena clutch her chest and collapse, and when Rham Jas lowered her to the floor and tried to save her, I knew she wasn’t breathing and no one could bring her back.

grounded_facts: Mrs. Ganush suddenly appears in the road, causing Ray to brake violently and the car to screech to a halt.
memories.memory_text: I suddenly appeared in the road, and I saw the car screech to a halt as Ray slammed on the brakes.

grounded_facts: The figure of Mrs. Ganush vanishes and is replaced by an ordinary old man who mutters and walks away.
memories.memory_text: I was there in the road, and then I was gone—replaced by an ordinary old man who muttered and walked away.

grounded_facts: Mrs. Ganush's hankie manifests supernaturally, obstructing Stephanie's vision and causing her to crash.
memories.memory_text: I made my hankie fly to block Stephanie's vision, flapping it over her eyes so she couldn't see and would crash.

grounded_facts: Stephanie's car crashes into a tree after being obstructed by Mrs. Ganush's hankie, which appears supernaturally on the windshield and then over her eyes.
memories.memory_text: I saw that Stephanie's car swerved and crashed into a tree after my hankie covered her eyes, though I wasn't sure if it was exactly how I intended it to happen.

grounded_facts: When Stephanie pulls on the corpse's hand, the body lurches up and wraps its arms around her in a violent embrace.
memories.memory_text: I lurched up when she pulled my hand, and my arms wrapped around her in a violent embrace.

grounded_facts: Stephanie locates and begins digging at the freshly buried grave of Mrs. Ganush in the cemetery during a rainy night.
memories.memory_text: I felt the force of her pulling at my hand, the pain as my body was wrenched from the coffin, and then the cold mud as I was thrown back—my arms had locked around her, but I had no will in it.

grounded_facts: Stephanie performs a ritual at Mrs. Ganush's grave to return the cursed button and break the supernatural curse.
memories.memory_text: I remember Stephanie speaking to me, saying she was giving the button back, declaring it as a formal gift to me, Sylvia Ganush, as if that would settle things. She grabbed my hand, forced my body to lurch up, and despite my dead arms wrapping around her, she pushed me away. In the end, she made her declaration again—formal, final—before leaving me in the mud.

grounded_facts: Stephanie verbally declares a formal gift of the button (in the envelope) to Mrs. Ganush and forces it into her mouth.
memories.memory_text: I was told that Stephanie formally gave the button in the envelope to me, and heard her say, 'Choke on it, bitch,' as she forced it toward me.

grounded_facts: After failing to place the envelope in the corpse's hand due to rigor mortis, Stephanie pries open the jaw and inserts the envelope into the corpse's throat.
memories.memory_text: I felt my jaw pried open and the envelope forced into my throat, then my jaw snapped shut, trapping it between my broken teeth.

grounded_facts: A surge of mud collapses into the grave, burying both Stephanie and the corpse, submerging them completely before Stephanie emerges.
memories.memory_text: I felt the mud surge around me as I was pushed down into the grave, my face pressed against Stephanie's, and then we were both submerged beneath the weight of the collapsing earth.

grounded_facts: Stephanie breaks through the surface of the mud, grabs a tree root, and pulls herself out of the grave, then staggers away.
memories.memory_text: I saw Stephanie break through the surface of the mud, grab a tree root, and pull herself out before staggering away into the rain.

grounded_facts: A scheduled class at UCLA where Ray Dalton lectures on the psychology of supernatural beliefs and their relation to abnormal behavior.
memories.memory_text: I was lecturing at UCLA about how the mind creates supernatural beliefs to explain uncertainty, and how those beliefs can become abnormal when they interfere with daily life.

grounded_facts: Ray concludes his lecture on the supernatural and psychological abnormality as the class bell rings.
memories.memory_text: I concluded my lecture and told the students we'd be covering clinical manifestations of psychosis tomorrow as the bell rang.

grounded_facts: Ray smiles upon seeing Stephanie enter the lecture hall with food.
memories.memory_text: I smiled when I saw Stephanie come in with the food.

grounded_facts: Stephanie enters the lecture hall holding a bag of deli food, interrupting Ray's post-lecture moment.
memories.memory_text: I saw Stephanie walk into the lecture hall holding a bag of deli food, interrupting my moment after class.

grounded_facts: Stephanie reveals uncertainty about her new position due to competition from another candidate.
memories.memory_text: I heard Stephanie say there's a new guy they're considering for the job too, which made her sound uncertain.

grounded_facts: Ray notices Stephanie's disappointment about a job competition and physically comforts her, affirming her qualifications.
memories.memory_text: I saw how disappointed Stephanie was about the job competition, so I held her and told her that they need someone with her experience.

grounded_facts: Stephanie visits Ray in his university office, where they discuss her job situation and exchange personal updates.
memories.memory_text: I remember Stephanie came to my office, we caught up while she ate a salad and I graded papers, and she gave me an old nickel from her purse after we talked about her job situation.

grounded_facts: Stephanie hands Ray an envelope containing a 1925 Indian Head nickel she obtained from a bank teller.
memories.memory_text: I remember Stephanie handing me an envelope, and when I opened it, I saw a 1925 Indian Head nickel she got from a bank teller—I recognized it right away and told her it was a good find before I put it in my pocket.

grounded_facts: Ray answers a speakerphone call from his mother, Trudy, and asks her to hold briefly.
memories.memory_text: I answered the speakerphone when my mom called and said, 'Hi Mom, can you hold on a sec?'

grounded_facts: Ray tells Stephanie he will call her tonight, indicating a plan to reconnect after their meeting.
memories.memory_text: I told Stephanie I'll call her tonight, so we can reconnect after our meeting.

grounded_facts: Ray informs his mother that Stephanie will come over for dinner tomorrow night to meet her and his father.
memories.memory_text: I told my mom that Stephanie is coming over for dinner tomorrow night to meet her and Dad.

grounded_facts: Trudy questions Stephanie's suitability based on her job and background, implying she does not meet family expectations.
memories.memory_text: I remember my mother questioning Stephanie's job as a bank teller and implying she wasn't good enough for me, like our family has higher expectations.

grounded_facts: Ray clearly states he is in a relationship with Stephanie and is not seeking anyone else, rejecting his mother's matchmaking.
Ray asserts his commitment to Stephanie despite his mother's pressure to date someone more socially suitable.

memories.memory_text: I was explaining how the mind creates the supernatural to cope with uncertainty when the bell rang, and I saw Stephanie walk in with food, which made me smile despite the abrupt end to my lecture.

I remember the way Stephanie handed me that old 1925 Indian Head nickel—she’d had it put in an envelope, like it meant something. I could tell she wanted to cheer me up, and I made sure to sound glad for it.
After Stephanie kissed me and left, I turned back to the phone and said, 'Hi Mom, can you hold on a sec?'
I cut my mom off on the phone when she started pushing me to call Julie Kulick—I told her I’m with Stephanie and not looking for anyone else, then ended the call.
I asked the officer about getting a restraining order for Stephanie, needing to know if there was a way to keep her safer right now.
I held Stephanie close when she shivered, feeling how upset she was about Mrs. Ganush, even though she said she was fine.
She suddenly got excited about getting our fortunes read and pulled me, still protesting, into that psychic shop.
I handed over my credit card, feeling uneasy as Rham Jas swiped it—sixty dollars for a fortune reading I didn’t believe in, but Stephanie wanted it, so I didn’t stop him.
I felt the air turn cold and saw the candle flicker, and when Rham Jas said a 'bad spirit' had come upon Stephanie, I couldn't explain it—but I knew something was wrong.

I remember Stephanie asking how the psychic could have known about her lost button, her voice tinged with wonder, and I told her it was just clever guessing — that he was playing her emotions to leave her with questions and his business card.
I walked with Stephanie from the car up the path to her house, the iron gate creaking as we pushed it open, the night air cool and quiet around us.
I kissed Stephanie before leaving, and from my car, I reminded her about dinner at my parents’ tomorrow night—we’re supposed to bring dessert, and she said she’d bake her special cake.
I remember handing Stephanie the frozen peas, watching her press them to her bloody lip, and feeling a chill when she said it wasn't the old woman—it was something she'd sent.
I remember the weight of the prescription in my hand after the doctor confirmed Stephanie had PTSD—her panic, the paranoia, all of it making sense in the worst way.
I pulled the blanket up around her shoulder after seeing the sedatives on the nightstand, and when she turned to me, I asked how she was doing.
I told her about the trip—Saturday morning train to Santa Barbara, my family’s cabin in the hills, just the two of us by the river, a fire, champagne, and real time to talk.

I felt her thrashing and saw her eyes wide with terror—she was screaming like she was being torn apart. I grabbed her shoulders and shook her gently, saying, 'Steph! Wake up!' until she finally came to.

She was trembling, saying the old woman was here and she couldn't wake up—I didn't know what to believe, but I could see the fear in her eyes. After she calmed a little, I told her about Doctor Rangervertz's availability, hoping it might help ground her.
I pulled up in front of the bank, the car coming to a stop as I got ready to go inside.

I had the window replaced last night—told Stephanie it still needs body work, but at least the car’s safer now. I could see she was trying to hold it together, so I reminded her it’s okay if it takes time to get over this.
I told Stephanie I liked her dress, after she stepped out of the car and turned for me—golden light on her, the kind of moment that feels like a beginning.

memories.memory_text: I froze by the water fountain when I heard Ray’s mom say, 'Stephanie? The one from the farm?'—her voice like cold glass—and then, 'she’s just a teller at some bank,' like that was all I was.
I said 'Wait' just before he turned away, my hand already fumbling with my purse—sixty dollars felt like too much, but I couldn't let him leave, not when I needed to know.
I pressed the frozen peas to my split lip, the cold stinging through Ray’s coat, and finally said the words I’d been holding back—'I didn’t tell you the whole story.'

I placed the document on the floor and offered her the pen, my hands shaking, hoping she’d sign so I could fix what I’d done—but her eyes locked onto mine like she could see every mistake I’d ever made.

I was sitting in my car, stuffing Oreos in my mouth like it would fix anything, and suddenly thought—'Who could help me?' That’s when I remembered the card, dug it out of my purse, and just... started driving.

I remember holding up the brass button from my coat, showing it to Rham Jas—he looked uneasy, like it was something vile, and I knew then it was cursed, that this tiny thing was why the Lamia would come for me on the third day.

I heard the gate shriek—just like before—and then the shadows in the room felt heavier, the air thick, and when I heard scratching at the door, I ran upstairs and locked myself in, heart pounding, knowing it was already coming.
I buried the heart in the corner of the garden and tossed the knife into the bushes when I heard Ellen coming.
When Ellen pointed to the red stain on my sleeve, I said it was tomato juice from making a salad—my voice didn’t shake, but I could feel my pulse in my throat.
I offered Trudy the harvest cake I made, telling her the milk has to be straight from the cow, warm and unpasteurized—then I saw her face tighten like she was about to be sick.
Ray introduced me as a loan officer in charge of small business and home loans, and said I was on a fast track for a promotion—right there at the dinner table, in front of his parents.

I started to talk about the big loan account I'm working on—the biggest my branch has ever handled—but I remember feeling exposed, like I had to prove myself all over again just to hold onto that chance.
I told Ray the truth about the thing coming for me, and when he still refused to believe—tried to say it was just stress—I knew I couldn't stay. I stepped into the car and left him standing there.
I begged Ilenka to help me, to take the curse off—I was on the ground, shaking, telling her I needed it gone. She just looked down and said it would never come off.
I saw the corpse's head turn toward me, those dead eyes staring, wide open—I didn't imagine it. It was looking right at me.
I kicked in Rham Jas' TV, glass cracking under my boot—he flinched, finally looking at me. I yelled about the hundred and seventy-nine dollars I wasted on his damn book.
I signed the receipt with my Mastercard, hand steady even though my chest was tight. When he asked for twenty thousand in cash by tomorrow, I just said, 'What would you need from me?'
I was trying to pack my stuff and asked Ellen if she had cash or credit I could use, but she kept pushing about the cat—I couldn’t let her go digging into that.
She said she found the knife and told me she was moving out. I told her fine and yelled after her as she left.

I asked Mr. Jacks for the contract, thinking it was just a formality, and then he told me the promotion was going to Stu—my hands went cold, and I could feel the tears starting before I even left his office.
I was just standing there, eating ice cream from the tub, staring at that pathetic pile of cash on the table when Ray walked in and said he paid Rham Jas—even though he doesn’t believe—because I do.

I remember standing there, the cold weight of the brass button in my palm, realizing it wasn’t over—Rham Jas said the Lamia can’t be banished, not by a medium, and that it would come for me before sunrise.

I remember him putting the button in an envelope, handing it to me like it meant something—saying I could give it away, that the curse would follow the owner, and suddenly I understood I might survive by passing it on.
I held the envelope in my hands and thought about telling Ray the truth, but instead I said it was over—just like that, I let myself believe we were safe.
I screamed when I saw her in the headlights—Mrs. Ganush, right in front of the car—then suddenly she was gone, replaced by an old man like nothing happened.
I told Ray the trip was still on, and that we should meet at the D station because I had something to do on the way.
I felt my chest tighten when I realized the envelope wasn't in my purse—then I found it under the seat, and I held it so tight, like it might vanish again.
I remember asking Rham Jas under that bare bulb, my voice tight—'Well? Is it possible?'—and pacing, waiting, the idea forming: if the soul never dies, maybe the dead can take the curse instead.
I remember gripping the cursed envelope in the car, raincoat zipped tight, thinking, 'I'll shove it down her goddamn throat'—like that would finally end it.
The hankie flew out of nowhere, slapped over my eyes—I couldn't see, just wind and cloth—and then the car swerved and slammed into a tree.
I jammed the shovel into her mouth and forced it open, mud pouring in as I shoved the envelope down her throat—she was going to take it back, no matter how dead she was.
I was buried up to my armpits, then completely under the mud. The corpse was pushed against me, her face against my cheek. I surfaced and pulled myself out by a tree root, gasping for air.

I was driving through the empty streets, my hair still damp from the shower, when Mr. Jacks' voice on the message said Stu broke down crying after they caught him stealing my file and trying to make his own deal—I felt the smile rise before I even realized it.

I remember the morning light just starting to break as I stepped out of my car, the weight of my weekend bag in my hand, and then Mr. Jacks’ voice on the phone saying the assistant manager’s position was mine.
I took Ray’s hand and told him I’d try to live up to his belief in me—finally feeling like I could start over, clean, with that old coat gone for good.

I saw the cursed button in Ray’s hand and couldn’t breathe. I backed away, but the train was coming. The whistle screamed like that sound I’ve heard before—the one from the dark. In the smoke, I saw the face. Then it hit me.

memories.memory_text: I placed the crumpled papers on her desk and asked, 'Will you help me?' My voice trembled, but I held my ground, watching her eyes scan the delinquency notice and the court order.
I lunged at her through the broken window, biting down on her chin—my gums grinding against her skin as she screamed and shoved me back.
I told her, 'You shamed me,' then took a button from her sleeve and said, 'The Lamia. It's coming for you.'
My shadow appeared on the wall when the car headlights passed, dark and clear, shaped like me, though I wasn't in the room.
I struck her face with unseen force, then reached up from the floor and touched her through the reflection before vanishing.
I shook her, my withered hands tight on her throat—she looked up at me, helpless, just like when she ruined me.
I lunged at her, covered in black flies, my teeth snapping—so close I could feel her breath, her fear—she tried to push me off but I was stronger, I was winning.
I scratch my nails across her desk, the sound sharp and slow—SCRATCH... SCRATCH...—and for a moment, she sees me, sees my yellowed hand where that man’s should be.
I saw her place that paper on the floor like I was some beggar, but I didn't look up—just held my mother’s photo tighter and said no. My hands shook, but my voice didn’t.
When she said she’d suffered enough, I laughed—really laughed—for the first time in years, my broken teeth showing. 'Not yet!' I screamed, and I could feel the dark thing inside me rise.
I hear my granddaughter speak my name to the crowd, declaring that the white trash farm girl bears the curse of Lamia—my curse, born from the shame and rage I carried when she cast me out.
Even in death, I feel myself rise—not with breath, not with life—but my head turns, my eyes open, and I fix my gaze on her, the one who cast me out, knowing she can see me now, finally understanding.
I stepped into the road, right into the headlights, making them see me—making them stop. The car screeched and I felt the power surge through me, knowing they could no longer ignore what they'd done.
When they looked again, I was gone—replaced by an old man muttering at them. I shifted, slipped away in form, still watching, still there, still coming for her.
I remember the weight of the earth pressing down, the silence of the grave—but still, I clawed at it, my will not done, my vengeance unspent.
I heard Rham Jas say the soul never dies, and that the curse could be given to someone who has passed on.
I felt my hankie tear loose and fly—slamming onto her windshield, flapping, then whipping across her face, stuck over her eyes as she screamed and the car spun out.
I felt the shovel pry my jaw open, cold metal forcing my teeth apart, and then the envelope shoved down my throat—I couldn't breathe, only swallow the curse back in.
I rose through the mud, my body drawn to hers, and pressed my face against Stephanie's cheek—grinning as we sank together, bound in the curse.
